speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Introduced the Excise Tariff Amendment (Tobacco) Bill 2014, outlining four staged 12.5 per cent tobacco excise increases from 1 December 2013 to 1 September 2016 and a shift in indexation from the consumer price index to wages from 1 March 2014, consistent with Australia's 2003 accession to the World Health Organization's Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Introduced the Customs Tariff Amendment (Tobacco) Bill 2014, applying the same staged 12.5 per cent duty increases on imported tobacco from 1 December 2013 to 1 September 2016 and the same shift in indexation to wages from 1 March 2014 that apply to locally produced tobacco.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Southcott
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, noting Australia's smoking rate has fallen 40 to 44 per cent over 30 years, and warned that illicit tobacco seizures reached 200 million sticks with a potential $151 million in duty evaded in 2012-13.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills as building on Labor's plain packaging reforms, noting smoking kills about six million people worldwide and over 15,000 Australians each year, and said the bills would raise the excise share of a cigarette pack's price to 62 per cent by 1 September 2016.

speeches.speaker: David Gillespie
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, saying the increases will raise $6.5 billion over the forward estimates, and cited a fall in the national smoking rate to 20 per cent, though Indigenous smoking rates remain around 49 per cent.

speeches.speaker: Amanda Rishworth
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, crediting Labor's plain packaging reform with a 78 per cent rise in calls to the Quitline, and highlighted the $14.5 million Indigenous Tobacco Control Initiative that funded projects in 18 Indigenous communities.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, saying smoking costs Australia $31.5 billion a year and kills 15,500 Australians annually, said daily smoking among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people fell from 51 per cent in 2002 to 41 per cent, and called on the National Party to follow Labor, which stopped accepting tobacco donations in 2004, and stop taking donations from tobacco companies.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, noting the 1 December excise increase added $1.23 to a packet of Winfield 25s taking the average price to $19.14, said the measure will deliver a net cash benefit of $370 million in the 2013 to 2014 financial year rising to $2.19 billion by 2016 to 2017, and warned it is a regressive tax that will harm the lowest socioeconomic groups.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, said Australia's smoking rate fell from 25 per cent in 1991 to just under 16 per cent in 2010 against a COAG target of 10 per cent by 2018, cited a 25 per cent excise rise in April 2010 that cut tobacco consumption by about 10.2 per cent, and said heart attack risk drops sharply within a year of quitting while lung cancer death risk halves after 10 years.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, said tobacco is responsible for 7.8 per cent of Australia's total disease burden and 15,551 deaths a year, said alcohol-related harm cost Australia an estimated $14.352 billion in 2010, and called for mandatory alcohol warning labels similar to tobacco's plain packaging regime.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, said tax makes up only 60 per cent of the cigarette price in Australia compared with 74 per cent in New Zealand, 77 per cent in the United Kingdom and 80 per cent in France, cited Treasury findings that the April 2010 25 per cent excise rise cut tobacco consumption by about 11 per cent, and said smoking costs Australia about $31 billion a year including 750,000 hospital bed days.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the tobacco excise bills, said Australia's tobacco excise is only 51 per cent of the retail price against a World Health Organization recommendation of at least 70 per cent, said the Liberal Party has accepted more than $3 million in tobacco donations since 1999, and said the National Party confirmed on 4 February that it was still accepting tobacco industry donations.
